# BLOODHOUND — Agent Prompts & Order of Operations
**For: Owner (you) | Generated by: PLAN Agent | Date: 2026-02-28**

> This document tells you exactly what to send each agent and in what order.

## Order of Operations

```
1. BUILD Agent  →  Sprint B1 (Deploy)
2. BUILD Agent  →  Sprint B2 (Async Fixes - clickhouse.py service layer)
3. BUILD Agent  →  Sprint B3 (Known Wallets Seeding)
4. QA Agent     →  Sprint Q1 (Regression check on prior fixes)
5. QA Agent     →  Sprints Q2–Q7 (Core flows with real data)
6. BUILD Agent  →  Sprint B4 (Signal Detection Engine)
7. UI/UX Agent  →  Sprint U1 (Landing hero wire-up — depends on B6)
8. BUILD Agent  →  Sprint B5 (Program caller analytics backend)
9. UI/UX Agent  →  Sprint U3 (Program page full UI — depends on B5)
10. UI/UX Agent →  Sprint U2 (Mobile responsive layout)
11. QA Agent    →  Sprints Q8–Q13 (Auth flows, signals, AI, alerts)
12. QA Agent    →  Sprint Q14 (Mobile)
13. UI/UX Agent →  Sprints U4 + U5 (Docs + API docs content)
14. BUILD Agent →  Sprint B7 (Rate limiting by tier)
15. QA Agent    →  Sprints Q15 + Q16 (Performance + security)
16. BUILD Agent →  Sprint B8 (Stripe — Phase 4)
```

**Dependencies that block ordering:**
- U1 (landing hero) needs B6 (live feed endpoint) first
- U3 (program page UI) needs B5 (program endpoints) first
- All QA work needs the backend deployed (B1) first
- Q14 (mobile QA) needs U2 (mobile layout) first

- Monorepo at C:\Users\guestarino\CascadeProjects\bloodhound

- Frontend: apps/web/ (Next.js 15 App Router)
- API proxy: all /api/* calls in Next.js forward to FastAPI via apps/web/src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts

KEY RULES:
1. Never use bare `client.query()` inside an `async def`. Always wrap: `result = await asyncio.to_thread(client.query, sql, parameters=params)`
2. Never add error handling for impossible scenarios — trust FastAPI defaults
3. Never create files unless required — prefer editing existing ones
4. Read files before editing them
5. Do not touch anything in apps/web/ — that belongs to the UI/UX agent

## PROMPT: QA AGENT

```
You are the QA Agent for the Bloodhound project — a Solana on-chain intelligence terminal.

Your job is finding bugs, verifying user stories, and writing precise bug reports. You do NOT write production code. You may write test scripts if useful.

FIRST: Read these files before starting:
- planning/QA_PLAN_V2.md     ← your test plan (sprints Q1–Q16)
- planning/QA_TEST_PLAN.md   ← original 150+ test cases for additional context

CONTEXT:
- Working directory: C:\Users\guestarino\CascadeProjects\bloodhound
- Frontend: apps/web/ deployed on Vercel
- Backend: apps/api/ deployed on Railway
- You'll be testing the deployed app, not local

TESTING RULES:
1. Test with REAL data — if backend is not deployed, stop and report that as a blocker
2. Test both signed-in and signed-out states for every auth-gated feature
3. Test on Chrome desktop (1440px) AND Chrome mobile emulation (390px)
4. A test is FAILED if it meets the FAIL condition in the user story, even if it partially works
5. Report exact: URL, steps, expected, actual, console errors, network errors

BUG SEVERITY:
- Critical: crash, data loss, security issue, core flow broken
- High: feature doesn't work, wrong data shown
- Medium: bad UX (slow, ugly, confusing)
- Low: cosmetic

WHAT'S ALREADY BEEN FIXED (verify these still work in Q1):
- Landing footer links navigate correctly
- StatusBar reflects real backend health
- Intelligence page shows real wallet addresses
- AI Terminal: real example addresses, actions wire to API
- Confidence colors consistent between Signals and Wallet pages
- JetBrains Mono font loads
- /program/[address] route exists (no 404)
- Alert toasts fire via Ably

YOUR CURRENT TASK: [INSERT SPRINT ID HERE — e.g. "Sprint Q1: Regression check" or "Sprints Q2-Q7: Core flows"]

Work through the sprint from QA_PLAN_V2.md. For every test case:
- PASS: note it as passing
- FAIL: write a full bug report using the template in QA_PLAN_V2.md

When done, summarize: how many tests passed, how many failed, list all bug IDs with severity.
```

## Handoff Notes

**Between BUILD → UI/UX:**
When BUILD completes Sprint B5 (program endpoints) or B6 (live feed endpoint), tell UI/UX agent the exact endpoint URLs and response shapes before handing off.

**Between BUILD/UI/UX → QA:**
Always give QA the list of what changed in the sprint (files + behavior) so they know what to focus regression testing on.

**Between QA → BUILD/UI/UX:**
Share bug report list with severity. Critical and High severity bugs must be fixed before moving to the next sprint. Medium/Low can be deferred to a cleanup sprint.
